sentences.en: So in 1913, he had asked 25 times if he could start a war with Serbia.
sentences.zh: 而弗朗茨·斐迪南基本上每次都阻止了他。

sentences.en: And basically Franz Ferdinand had blocked him at every opportunity.
sentences.zh: 但在弗朗茨·斐迪南死后的几个小时内，他说，太棒了，机会来了。

sentences.en: But within hours of Franz Ferdinand's death, he says, brilliant, this is the opportunity.
sentences.zh: 多么讽刺啊。

sentences.en: What an irony.
sentences.zh: 那个一直阻止我的人，我竟然可以用他的死作为借口。

sentences.en: The one guy who was stopping me, I can use his death as the pretext.
sentences.zh: 那个阻碍我的人，我可以借他的死作为借口。

sentences.en: And he said to the foreign minister of Austria,
sentences.zh: 他对奥地利外交部长说，

sentences.en: Count Bergthold, you know, we have a poisonous adder at our heel and we need to stamp on its head.
sentences.zh: 伯希托德伯爵，你知道，我们脚后跟有一条毒蛇，我们必须踩碎它的头。

sentences.en: And Bergthold, I think we quoted this in the Franz Ferdinand series, later wrote, with a faraway look of melancholy on his fine featured face, he concluded emphatically with three
sentences.zh: 我想我们在弗朗茨·斐迪南系列节目中引用过，伯希托德后来写道，他那张轮廓分明的脸上带着一种忧郁而遥远的表情，斩钉截铁地说了三个

sentences.en: words, war, war, war.
sentences.zh: 词：战争，战争，战争。

sentences.en: So there's never been any conspiracy theory that he was behind the murder of Franz Ferdinand.
sentences.zh: 所以从来没有任何阴谋论说他是弗朗茨·斐迪南遇刺案的幕后黑手。

sentences.en: Gosh, that's a good idea.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这主意不错。

sentences.en: It's a good one, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 是个好主意，不是吗？

sentences.en: Well, maybe that could be the conspiracy that our team of crack detectives will be introducing in the second half of the show.
sentences.zh: 嗯，也许这正是我们那支神探团队在节目下半部分要引入的阴谋。

sentences.en: They can investigate that.
sentences.zh: 他们可以去调查一下。

sentences.en: That's the season finale, surely.
sentences.zh: 那肯定是季终集的内容。

sentences.en: Yeah, that is exciting news for listeners.
sentences.zh: 没错，这对听众来说是个令人兴奋的消息。

sentences.en: What's coming in the second half?
sentences.zh: 下半部分会有什么内容？

sentences.en: You'll be surprised.
sentences.zh: 你会感到惊讶的。

sentences.en: Well, you won't if you've heard the previous episode, but newcomers will be surprised.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你听过上一集就不会了，但新听众会感到惊讶的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: So the Austrians send their ultimatum on 23rd of July.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人在7月23日发出了最后通牒。

sentences.en: The Serbs reject the key demands, and on the 28th of July, Franz Josef signs the declaration of war.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚人拒绝了关键要求，7月28日，弗朗茨·约瑟夫签署了宣战书。

sentences.en: Now, the mad thing about the Austrians is they are conscious that the Serbs have this gigantic patron and protector in Russia, but they really give Russia no thought at all.
sentences.zh: 现在，奥地利人疯狂的地方在于，他们意识到塞尔维亚人在俄罗斯有这样一个庞大的靠山和保护者，但他们根本没把俄罗斯放在眼里。

sentences.en: They don't send any troops to their eastern border.
sentences.zh: 他们没有向东部边境派遣任何军队。

sentences.en: Conrad's hope is that basically the Germans will either deter the Russians, or in the worst case scenario, if the Russians join the war, the Germans will deal with them.
sentences.zh: 康拉德的希望基本上是德国人要么能威慑住俄国人，要么在最坏的情况下，如果俄国人参战，德国人会去对付他们。

sentences.en: All he's thinking about is the spectacular victory that he's going to win over Serbia.
sentences.zh: 他满脑子想的都是他即将在塞尔维亚取得的辉煌胜利。

sentences.en: The question, though, of course, is, is Austria going to get a win?
sentences.zh: 然而，问题当然是，奥地利真的能赢吗？

sentences.en: I mean, this is the weird thing.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这才是最奇怪的地方。

sentences.en: The Austrians haven't really given any thought to whether they actually win such a war.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人根本没考虑过他们是否真的能赢得这样一场战争。

sentences.en: So they have 40 infantry divisions, the Austrians.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人有40个步兵师。

sentences.en: The Serbs have 11.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚人有11个。

sentences.en: The Serbs' population is much smaller.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚的人口要少得多。

sentences.en: Oddly, relative to population, the Serbs have more troops, but the Austrians have more in absolute numbers.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，相对于人口而言，塞尔维亚人的军队比例更高，但奥地利人的绝对数量更多。

sentences.en: The Austrians have quite good weapons, but not enough of them.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人的武器相当不错，但数量不足。

sentences.en: And the reason they don't have enough of them is because before the war, there'd been this endless, endless budget squabbling with the Hungarian parliament.
sentences.zh: 他们武器不足的原因是，在战争爆发前，他们与匈牙利议会进行了没完没了的预算争吵。

sentences.en: And that, I think, tells its own story about Austria-Hungary's greatest military problem, which is basically diversity is not its strength.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这本身就说明了奥匈帝国最大的军事问题，那就是多元化并非其优势。

sentences.en: So most of the men don't even speak the same language.
sentences.zh: 大多数士兵甚至语言都不通。

sentences.en: Most of the officers speak German.
sentences.zh: 大多数军官说德语。

sentences.en: And there's actually been huge arguments about whether that should continue or not.
sentences.zh: 关于是否应该继续保持这种情况，其实一直存在巨大的争议。

sentences.en: You know, is it right that all officers have to speak German?
sentences.zh: 你知道，所有军官都必须说德语，这合理吗？

sentences.en: But out of every 100 soldiers in the Austro-Hungarian army, 26 speak German, 23 Hungarian, 13 Czech,
sentences.zh: 但在奥匈帝国军队中，每100名士兵里，26人说德语，23人说匈牙利语，13人说捷克语，

sentences.en: 9 Serbian or Croat, 8 speak Polish, 8 are Ukrainian, 7 are Romanians, 4 are Slovaks, and 2 are Slovenians.
sentences.zh: 9人说塞尔维亚语或克罗地亚语，8人说波兰语，8人说乌克兰语，7人说罗马尼亚语，4人说斯洛伐克语，2人说斯洛文尼亚语。

sentences.en: And I'm sure there's also a category that's just this other, Roma.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定还有一个类别就是“其他”，比如罗姆人。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错，正是如此。

sentences.en: Or Jews who speak Yiddish or something.
sentences.zh: 或者是说意第绪语的犹太人什么的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So in other words, you know, this is a sort of a real ragbag kind of, it's a Tower of Babel,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，这简直是个大杂烩，是个巴别塔，

sentences.en: Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆。

sentences.en: It's a traveling Tower of Babel.
sentences.zh: 这是一个移动的巴别塔。

sentences.en: Conrad thinks, well, that's not a problem.
sentences.zh: 康拉德认为，嗯，那不是问题。

sentences.en: We can overcome this.
sentences.zh: 我们可以克服这一点。

sentences.en: He had written many times before the war, in 1890, for example, he had written that leadership is all about swift decision-making and strength of will.
sentences.zh: 他在战前写过很多次，例如在1890年，他写道领导力全在于迅速的决策和意志力。

sentences.en: All you need is strength of will.
sentences.zh: 你所需要的只是意志力。

sentences.en: I mean, actually, the Austrians don't really have either of those things.
sentences.zh: 我是说，实际上，奥地利人这两样东西都没有。

sentences.en: They're incredibly slow decision-makers.
sentences.zh: 他们的决策速度慢得惊人。

sentences.en: And as I remember, don't they also have a massively complicated railway system that prevents them from moving troops rapidly across their territories?
sentences.zh: 我记得，他们不是还有一个极其复杂的铁路系统，阻碍了他们在领土内快速调动军队吗？

sentences.en: Yes, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: Which is what Conrad should have been studying rather than writing letters to Gina, one might argue.
sentences.zh: 有人可能会说，康拉德应该研究这个，而不是给吉娜写信。

sentences.en: Well, every way in which they organize this war is laughable.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们组织这场战争的每一个环节都令人发笑。

sentences.en: Here's a perfect example, right?
sentences.zh: 这有个完美的例子，对吧？

sentences.en: The morning after the declaration war, the early hours of the 29th of July, they say, well, we're going to kick off the campaign.
sentences.zh: 宣战后的第二天早上，即7月29日凌晨，他们说，好吧，我们要开始行动了。

sentences.en: And they have this river warship called the Bodrog.
sentences.zh: 他们有一艘叫“博德罗格”号的内河战舰。

sentences.en: Great name.
sentences.zh: 好名字。

sentences.en: Which begins firing shells across the Danube into the center of Belgrade.
sentences.zh: 它开始向多瑙河对岸的贝尔格莱德市中心发射炮弹。

sentences.en: So you think, okay, well, it's all going to kick off.
sentences.zh: 所以你会想，好吧，一切都要开始了。

sentences.en: But then the Austrians do absolutely nothing.
sentences.zh: 但随后奥地利人什么也没做。

sentences.en: So they then do nothing for two weeks.
sentences.zh: 他们就这样什么都没做，持续了两周。

sentences.en: And the reason for that is that Conrad, to please the kind of farming lobby in the empire, had introduced harvest leave for the army.
sentences.zh: 原因在于，康拉德为了取悦帝国境内的农业游说团体，为军队引入了收割假。

sentences.en: So all his men are away, like literally working in the sort of Thomas Hardy with their scythes.
sentences.zh: 所以他所有的士兵都离开了，就像托马斯·哈代小说里那样，拿着镰刀在干活。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And like a Thomas Hardy novel, they're kind of scything corn or wheat or whatever they're doing.
sentences.zh: 就像托马斯·哈代的小说一样，他们在那儿收割玉米或小麦，或者做着类似的事情。

sentences.en: And the troops from places like Zagreb and Budapest won't get back until the end of July.
sentences.zh: 而来自萨格勒布和布达佩斯等地的部队要到7月底才能回来。

sentences.en: So basically, the Serbs have all this time to get organized.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，塞尔维亚人有充足的时间来组织防御。

sentences.en: They've got two weeks to get organized.
sentences.zh: 他们有两周的时间来准备。

sentences.en: And here is the maddest part of this story.
sentences.zh: 这是这个故事中最疯狂的部分。

sentences.en: The man that the Serbs want to lead their armies, lead the resistance, is a man called Radomir
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚人想要领导军队、领导抵抗运动的人，是一个叫拉多米尔的人，

sentences.en: Putnik.
sentences.zh: 普特尼克。

sentences.en: And he had led their armies in the Balkan Wars.
sentences.zh: 他曾在巴尔干战争中领导过他们的军队。

sentences.en: So the wars they'd fought against the Ottoman Empire and then Bulgaria just before the First
sentences.zh: 也就是他们在第一次世界大战前夕与奥斯曼帝国和保加利亚打的那几场仗。

sentences.en: World War.
sentences.zh: 世界大战。

sentences.en: And Radomir Putnik, everybody loves Radomir Putnik in Serbia.
sentences.zh: 在塞尔维亚，每个人都爱戴拉多米尔·普特尼克。

sentences.en: He's in his late 60s.
sentences.zh: 他已经快70岁了。

sentences.en: He's got a huge white beard.
sentences.zh: 他留着一把巨大的白胡子。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And he's got chronic emphysema.
sentences.zh: 而且他患有慢性肺气肿。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So he's basically, he's a peak First World War general.
sentences.zh: 所以他基本上是第一次世界大战期间的巅峰将军。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: But also, he's been smoking those kind of really acrid, heavy Balkan cigarettes.
sentences.zh: 而且，他一直抽那种非常刺鼻、浓烈的巴尔干香烟。

sentences.en: The kind you love when you're hanging out in the cafes of BuchareSt.
sentences.zh: 就是你在布加勒斯特的咖啡馆里消磨时光时喜欢抽的那种。

sentences.en: Now, here's the thing, right?
sentences.zh: 现在，重点来了，对吧？

sentences.en: Where has he been?
sentences.zh: 他在哪儿呢？

sentences.en: Of course, he's been taking the waters at a spa while this has been going on.
sentences.zh: 当然，当这一切发生时，他正在温泉疗养地疗养。

sentences.en: And in all places, in the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
sentences.zh: 而且还是在奥匈帝国境内。

sentences.en: So this bloke Putnik has been at a spa called Bad Gleichenberg, which is in Bohemia.
sentences.zh: 所以这个叫普特尼克的家伙当时正在波希米亚一个叫巴特格莱兴贝格的温泉疗养地。

sentences.en: He finds out there's going to be a war.
sentences.zh: 他发现要打仗了。

sentences.en: He says, oh, I better get home.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，我最好回家。

sentences.en: He gets on the train and he's literally changing trains in Budapest when he's arrested by the Austro-Hungarians.
sentences.zh: 他上了火车，在布达佩斯换乘时被奥匈帝国当局逮捕了。

sentences.en: And this, I think, is the ultimate sign of the Austro-Hungarian lack of seriousness.
sentences.zh: 我认为，这是奥匈帝国缺乏严肃性的终极体现。

sentences.en: They've arrested this guy who's going to lead Serbia's armies against them.
sentences.zh: 他们逮捕了这个将要领导塞尔维亚军队对抗他们的人。

sentences.en: And when Franz Josef hears about this, he says, oh, this is very poor form.
sentences.zh: 当弗朗茨·约瑟夫听说这件事时，他说，哦，这太失礼了。

sentences.en: You can't arrest this guy.
sentences.zh: 你不能逮捕这个人。

sentences.en: Let him go home.
sentences.zh: 让他回家吧。

sentences.en: It's chivalrous.
sentences.zh: 这很有骑士风度。

sentences.en: So do you know what they do?
sentences.zh: 你知道他们做了什么吗？

sentences.en: They literally put him on a train to go home.
sentences.zh: 他们真的让他坐火车回家了。

sentences.en: Now, it takes him an eternity to actually get home.
sentences.zh: 现在，他花了很长时间才真正回到家。

sentences.en: I mean, on one level, it reflects tremendously well on the Austro-Hungarian Empire.
sentences.zh: 从某种程度上说，这在很大程度上反映了奥匈帝国的风度。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: On another level, what were they thinking?
sentences.zh: 但从另一方面看，他们到底在想什么？

sentences.en: I don't think the British would have done that with Napoleon.
sentences.zh: 我不认为英国人会对拿破仑做这种事。

sentences.en: Do you?
sentences.zh: 你觉得呢？

sentences.en: Well, would they have done that with Michael Collins?
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们会对迈克尔·柯林斯做这种事吗？

sentences.en: No, I don't think they would.
sentences.zh: 不，我不认为他们会。

sentences.en: Although they did, no, because they did arrest Eamon de Valera and then let him go.
sentences.zh: 虽然他们确实逮捕过埃蒙·德·瓦莱拉，然后又放了他。

sentences.en: Then he locked him up in Lincoln Jail.
sentences.zh: 后来又把他关进了林肯监狱。

sentences.en: Yeah, but later on, they arrested him by accident and let him go when the truce was going on, all the truce negotiations.
sentences.zh: 是的，但后来他们意外地逮捕了他，并在停火协议谈判期间放了他。

sentences.en: Oh, well, that's fair enough, if it's a truce.
sentences.zh: 哦，好吧，如果是停火，那还算合理。

sentences.en: Yet another opportunity to praise our beloved country, Tom.
sentences.zh: 又是一个赞美我们伟大祖国的机会，汤姆。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: Well done.
sentences.zh: 干得好。

sentences.en: You handled that beautifully.
sentences.zh: 你处理得非常漂亮。

sentences.en: Anyway, it takes him ages to get home.
sentences.zh: 总之，他花了很长时间才回到家。

sentences.en: The other Serbian officers basically have to blow open his safe to find out what his plans are.
sentences.zh: 其他塞尔维亚军官基本上不得不炸开他的保险箱，才能找到他的作战计划。

sentences.en: They read his plans.
sentences.zh: 他们读了他的计划。

sentences.en: His plans are, we won't engage the Austrians on the border.
sentences.zh: 他的计划是，我们不会在边境与奥地利人交战。

sentences.en: We'll actually withdraw from Belgrade and we'll wait for the Austrians to move before reacting.
sentences.zh: 我们实际上会从贝尔格莱德撤退，等待奥地利人行动后再做出反应。

sentences.en: So the Serbs are, on paper, massive underdogs in this war.
sentences.zh: 所以，在纸面上，塞尔维亚人在这场战争中是绝对的弱势群体。

sentences.en: I mean, this is the war the First World War is all about.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这就是第一次世界大战的本质。

sentences.en: And nobody really knows anything about it.
sentences.zh: 而且没人真正了解它。

sentences.en: The Serbs have about 200,000 men, but they've just fought in the Balkan Wars.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚人大约有20万军队，但他们刚刚打完巴尔干战争。

sentences.en: Very vicious wars, actually, in which they didn't necessarily cover themselves with, certainly not moral glory.
sentences.zh: 那是非常残酷的战争，实际上，他们并没有在其中获得什么，当然更谈不上道德上的荣耀。

sentences.en: They haven't really got any uniforms left.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎没有剩下的制服了。

sentences.en: Everyone says they look like tramps and scarecrows.
sentences.zh: 每个人都说他们看起来像流浪汉和稻草人。

sentences.en: They're sort of very battered looking, but they're famously stoical, the Serbian soldiers.
sentences.zh: 他们看起来非常破烂，但塞尔维亚士兵以坚忍著称。

sentences.en: And they can melt into the mountains, can't they?
sentences.zh: 他们能融入山中，不是吗？

sentences.en: They can melt into the mountains.
sentences.zh: 他们能融入山中。

sentences.en: The historian Nick Lloyd, who's just written a brilliant book on the Eastern Front, he quotes one guy who said, if you give the Serbian soldier bread and an onion, he's satisfied.
sentences.zh: 历史学家尼克·劳埃德刚刚写了一本关于东线的精彩著作，他引用了一个人的话，说如果你给塞尔维亚士兵面包和洋葱，他就满足了。

sentences.en: And is that your experience?
sentences.zh: 这是你的经验吗？

sentences.en: Would you concur with that?
sentences.zh: 你同意这一点吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think so.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想是的。

sentences.en: I think that's absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我认为这绝对正确。

sentences.en: I mean, in my experience, they were always eating onions and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我是说，根据我的经验，他们总是吃洋葱之类的东西。

sentences.en: They love it.
sentences.zh: 他们很喜欢。

sentences.en: They're also, they're very fierce.
sentences.zh: 他们也非常凶猛。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a terrible, this is now generating an absolute sort of bull can stereotype 101.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这太糟糕了，这简直是在制造最典型的巴尔干刻板印象。

sentences.en: But yeah.
sentences.zh: 但确实如此。

sentences.en: The Michael Palin of...
sentences.zh: 迈克尔·佩林式的……

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.en: The Serbs are a proud, rugged people.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚人是一个骄傲、坚韧的民族。

sentences.en: Basically, you're fighting the Serbs.
sentences.zh: 基本上，你在和塞尔维亚人作战。

sentences.en: He said, thirsty, thirsty, thirsty.

sentences.zh: 在奥地利人看来，情况更加恶化，因为塞尔维亚人，即使是正规军，由于没有制服了，看起来就像土匪。

sentences.en: Now, the Austrians do not take this lying down.
sentences.zh: 现在，奥地利人可不会坐以待毙。

sentences.zh: 现在我们谈到了东线的一个重大特征，无论它发生在何处，实际上都是如此。

sentences.zh: 他们射杀任何他们认为与游击活动有哪怕一点点联系的人。

sentences.zh: 现在，我必须说，在有人开始为塞尔维亚人流泪之前，塞尔维亚人在三年前的巴尔干战争中确实丢尽了脸面。

sentences.en: I mean, they had behaved really atrociously in Kosovo and Macedonia and so on.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他们在科索沃和马其顿等地表现得非常残暴。

sentences.en: What they've sowed, they are now reaping to some extent.
sentences.zh: 他们种下了什么，现在就在某种程度上收获了什么。

sentences.en: Can I just ask, in Belgium, when the Germans commit atrocities against civilians, this is obviously bad news for Germany's reputation and therefore in the long run

sentences.en: for their ability to prosecute the war.

sentences.zh: 他非常直白地描述了这一点。

sentences.en: He says,

sentences.zh: 对我们的仇恨是无限的，每个人都是我们的敌人。

sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，奥匈帝国的军官们自己也为此感到困扰。

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, the Austrians have been marching into Serbia.
sentences.zh: 现在，与此同时，奥地利人一直在向塞尔维亚进军。

sentences.en: They have a particular objective in mind, which is this railway junction at a place called Valjevo.
sentences.zh: 他们心中有一个特定的目标，那就是位于一个叫瓦列沃的地方的铁路枢纽。

sentences.en: And in the way, there is this kind of heavily forested ridge called Mount Sur.
sentences.zh: 在那条路上，有一道森林茂密的山脊，叫苏尔山。

sentences.en: And they reach the top on the late afternoon of the 15th of AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 他们在8月15日傍晚抵达了山顶。

sentences.en: They're knackered.
sentences.zh: 他们累坏了。

sentences.en: They're very thirsty.
sentences.zh: 他们渴极了。

sentences.en: They're very hungry.
sentences.zh: 他们饿极了。

sentences.en: There's a massive thunderstorm that night.
sentences.zh: 那天晚上爆发了一场巨大的雷暴。

sentences.en: And in the middle of the thunderstorm, that's the point that the Serbs choose to strike back.
sentences.zh: 就在雷暴正猛的时候，塞尔维亚人选择了反击。

sentences.en: And the result is total chaos.
sentences.zh: 结果是一片混乱。

sentences.en: The Austrians are inexperienced.
sentences.zh: 奥地利军队缺乏经验。

sentences.en: They panic.
sentences.zh: 他们惊慌失措。

sentences.en: They start running away.
sentences.zh: 他们开始逃跑。

sentences.en: They're kind of a huge mob of Austrians running away down this mountain.
sentences.zh: 他们就像一大群溃兵，顺着山坡逃窜。

sentences.en: And unbelievably, they just keep running.
sentences.zh: 令人难以置信的是，他们一直在跑。

sentences.en: And within four days, they've crossed the river again.
sentences.zh: 四天之内，他们又渡过了那条河。

sentences.en: And they've gone back to Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 他们退回了波斯尼亚。

sentences.en: So their first attempt to invade Serbia has been a ludicrous failure and a very bloody failure.
sentences.zh: 所以，他们第一次入侵塞尔维亚的尝试是一场荒唐且惨烈的失败。

sentences.en: The Serbs have lost 16,000 men.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚人损失了1.6万人。

sentences.en: The Austrians have lost 30,000, including loads and loads of their officers.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人损失了3万人，其中包括大量的军官。

sentences.en: And in the eyes of the world, this is a terrible humiliation for them.
sentences.zh: 在世人眼中，这对他们来说是极大的羞辱。

sentences.en: General Pottyorek has spent the whole time in Sarajevo, ironically.
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，波蒂奥雷克将军整个过程都待在萨拉热窝。

sentences.en: He says, oh, well, this wasn't my fault at all.
sentences.zh: 他说，哦，好吧，这根本不是我的错。

sentences.en: I think it was the fault of our Czech troops, actually.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这其实是我们捷克部队的错。

sentences.en: They're very disloyal.
sentences.zh: 他们很不忠诚。

sentences.en: They're poorly behaved, the Czechs.
sentences.zh: 捷克人表现得很差劲。

sentences.en: By blaming the Czechs, he's able to cling on to his job.
sentences.zh: 通过指责捷克人，他得以保住了自己的职位。

sentences.en: And straight away, he starts writing to Conrad.
sentences.zh: 他立刻开始给康拉德写信。

sentences.en: And he says, I'd love to have another crack at the Serbs.
sentences.zh: 他说，我很想再试着打一次塞尔维亚人。

sentences.en: Will you send me some more men and some more guns and whatnot?
sentences.zh: 你能再给我派些人、多给些枪之类的吗？

sentences.en: Conrad says, no, I don't think so.
sentences.zh: 康拉德说，不，我不这么认为。

sentences.en: You've had your chance.
sentences.zh: 你已经试过了。

sentences.en: But Pottyorek is well-connected at court.
sentences.zh: 但波蒂奥雷克在宫廷里关系很广。

sentences.en: He gets his friends to lobby the Emperor Franz Josef.
sentences.zh: 他找朋友去游说弗朗茨·约瑟夫皇帝。

sentences.en: And eventually, he's given permission to have another crack at the Serbs.
sentences.zh: 最终，他获准再次进攻塞尔维亚。

sentences.en: So, at dawn on the 14th of September, he has a second go.
sentences.zh: 于是，在9月14日黎明，他进行了第二次尝试。

sentences.en: Once again, they cross the rivers into Serbia from Bosnia.
sentences.zh: 他们再次从波斯尼亚渡河进入塞尔维亚。

sentences.en: This time, the Serbs have dug trenches.
sentences.zh: 这一次，塞尔维亚人挖了战壕。

sentences.en: And it degenerates quite quickly into kind of bloody hand-to-hand trench warfare.
sentences.zh: 战局很快演变成了血腥的近身战壕战。

sentences.en: The Austrians are thrown back.
sentences.zh: 奥地利军队被击退了。

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.zh: 噢，不。

sentences.en: It was not quite as chaotically as before.
sentences.zh: 这次不像上次那么混乱。

sentences.en: They say, well, we'll have another go.
sentences.zh: 他们说，好吧，我们再试一次。

sentences.en: So, in November, they have attempt number three.
sentences.zh: 于是，在11月，他们进行了第三次尝试。

sentences.en: Now, at this point, the Serbs are absolutely exhausted themselves.
sentences.zh: 此时，塞尔维亚人自己也已经精疲力竭了。

sentences.en: And they're running out of shells.
sentences.zh: 他们的炮弹也快用光了。

sentences.en: They haven't got any artillery.
sentences.zh: 他们没有任何炮兵支援。

sentences.en: They can't really rest their troops because they're running out of men.
sentences.zh: 他们无法让部队休息，因为兵力不足。

sentences.en: So, slowly, painfully, the Austrians are able to inch their way forward.
sentences.zh: 所以，奥地利人缓慢而痛苦地向前推进了一点点。

sentences.en: And the Serbs have to abandon Belgrade.
sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚人不得不放弃贝尔格莱德。

sentences.en: And they take up a new defensive line on a river called the Kolubara, which is deep inside central Serbia.
sentences.zh: 他们在塞尔维亚中部深处的一条叫科卢巴拉的河边建立了新的防线。

sentences.en: So, at this point, the Austrians, foolishly, I think, Tom, decide to celebrate victory.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我觉得奥地利人愚蠢地决定庆祝胜利。

sentences.en: They have premature victory celebrations.
sentences.zh: 他们举行了过早的胜利庆祝活动。

sentences.en: The Emperor sends Potiorik a message of congratulations.
sentences.zh: 皇帝给波蒂奥雷克发去了贺电。

sentences.en: Lots of towns name him an honorary citizen.
sentences.zh: 许多城镇授予他荣誉市民称号。

sentences.zh: 萨拉热窝的一条街道以他的名字重新命名。

sentences.zh: 这个人基本上，他的愚蠢导致了这一切。

sentences.en: It's caused the First World War, yeah.
sentences.zh: 这导致了第一次世界大战，没错。

sentences.zh: 然而，你可能会惊讶地发现，奥地利人可能高兴得太早了。

sentences.en: Because that guy who they'd released, the bloke with the beard, an emphysema, Radomir Putnik, his emphysema has gotten far worse under the pressure water.
sentences.zh: 因为那个被他们释放的留着胡子、患有肺气肿的拉多米尔·普特尼克，他的肺气肿在战争压力下变得更严重了。

sentences.en: So, he can't breathe.
sentences.zh: 所以，他呼吸困难。

sentences.en: We will not surrender.
sentences.zh: 我们绝不投降。

sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.zh: 但尽管他呼吸困难，他依然比任何奥地利指挥官都要出色得多。

sentences.en: So, he knows that the Austrians have now, they've gone on the attack.
sentences.zh: 他知道奥地利人现在已经发起了进攻。

sentences.zh: 他们没有任何食物。

sentences.en: They're ravaged by lice.
sentences.zh: 他们饱受虱子困扰。

sentences.en: They're miles ahead of their supply lines.
sentences.zh: 他们远离补给线。

sentences.en: They've got no shoes.
sentences.zh: 他们连鞋子都没有。

sentences.en: Their fancy uniforms are in rags.
sentences.zh: 他们华丽的制服已经破烂不堪。

sentences.en: They're very miserable.
sentences.zh: 他们非常悲惨。

sentences.en: And actually, the weather has now changed.
sentences.zh: 而且实际上，天气现在变了。

sentences.en: So, having been very...
sentences.zh: 所以，在经历了非常……

sentences.zh: 这就是东线战场的情况。

sentences.en: There's only two weather settings.
sentences.zh: 天气只有两种模式。

sentences.en: It's either unbelievably, suffocatingly hot, or you're dying of, you know...
sentences.zh: 要么是热得令人窒息，要么就是快要死于……

sentences.en: Frostbite.
sentences.zh: 冻伤。

sentences.zh: 没错，冻伤。

sentences.en: So, now it's snowing.
sentences.zh: 所以，现在下雪了。

sentences.en: And meanwhile, Putnik has done something amazing.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，普特尼克做了一件了不起的事。

sentences.zh: 他安排法国人通过萨洛尼卡（塞萨洛尼基）运来了1.1万发炮弹。

sentences.en: They're the wrong size for the Serbian guns.
sentences.zh: 这些炮弹的尺寸和塞尔维亚火炮的不匹配。

sentences.zh: 所以，每一枚炮弹都必须拆开、重新组装，再运到前线。

sentences.zh: 11月下旬，普特尼克集结了他的部队。

sentences.zh: 他基本上召集了所有塞尔维亚男人。

sentences.zh: 总共有20万人。

sentences.zh: 他有400门火炮。

sentences.zh: 而且他有一个秘密武器。

sentences.zh: 那是什么，多米尼克？

sentences.zh: 这个秘密武器是一个人。

sentences.zh: 他是塞尔维亚国王彼得·卡拉乔尔杰维奇。

sentences.zh: 塞尔维亚国王。

sentences.zh: 多米尼克，我大胆猜一下。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 根据我之前了解到的第一次世界大战初期重要人物的信息，

sentences.zh: 我猜他年纪很大了。

sentences.zh: 我猜他非常忧郁。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 而且我猜他患有某种严重的疾病。

sentences.zh: 我猜对了吗？

sentences.zh: 他患有风湿病。

sentences.zh: 不过，如果你谷歌一下他，他确实留着一撇很棒的胡子。

sentences.zh: 而且他年纪很大？

sentences.zh: 是的，他70岁了。

sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.zh: 总之，彼得国王巡视了战壕。

sentences.en: And he says,
sentences.zh: 他说，

sentences.en: My children, I have learned that some among your number tire of fighting.
sentences.zh: 我的孩子们，我听说你们当中有些人厌倦了战斗。

sentences.en: But I, I shall stay to the end.
sentences.zh: 但我，我将坚持到底。

sentences.en: A French reporter who was there said of the Serbs, I'm sure this is true.
sentences.zh: 一位在场的法国记者谈到塞尔维亚人时说，我相信这是真的。

sentences.en: Each of them felt his soul gripped with a furious desire to seize victory or to die for their old uncle, who had stayed there among his children in spite of his failing health,
sentences.zh: 他们每个人都感到灵魂被一种强烈的渴望所攫住，那就是为了他们的老叔叔而夺取胜利或牺牲，尽管健康状况不佳，他依然待在孩子们中间，

sentences.en: even as the cannons roared and the bullets whistled.
sentences.zh: 即便炮声隆隆，子弹呼啸。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这很有趣，不是吗？它反映了西线战场的模式，即德国人过度拉长了补给线。

sentences.en: There's an elderly man who says we're going to fight.
sentences.zh: 有一位老人说我们要战斗到底。

sentences.en: Yeah.

sentences.zh: 反攻开始了。

sentences.zh: 那就是防御能力远大于进攻部队突破这些防御的能力，你觉得呢？

sentences.zh: 我觉得这绝对是真的。

sentences.zh: 还有战壕之类的东西。

sentences.en: Completely true.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.zh: 然而，我认为任何写过奥地利在战争中表现的人，比如尼克·劳埃德或亚历山大·沃森，无论他们的书里怎么写，

sentences.en: they unanimously agree that the Austrian performance is absolutely risible.
sentences.zh: 他们一致认为奥地利军队的表现简直可笑至极。

sentences.zh: 总之，塞尔维亚人在1914年12月3日早晨发起了反攻。

sentences.en: It's a foggy, snowy morning.
sentences.zh: 那是一个大雾弥漫、白雪皑皑的早晨。

sentences.en: They start with the shells that the Austrians weren't expecting.
sentences.zh: 他们先用奥地利人意想不到的炮弹进行轰击。

sentences.zh: 然后他们发起了冲锋。

sentences.en: There's a brilliant description, actually, in Nick Lloyd's Eastern Front book.

sentences.en: The battle goes on into the night.
sentences.zh: 战斗一直持续到深夜。

sentences.zh: 到处是手榴弹爆炸的声音。

sentences.zh: 到处是冲锋的部队。

sentences.en: There's machine gun fire.
sentences.zh: 到处是机枪扫射的声音。

sentences.en: The Austrians are losing more and more men.
sentences.zh: 奥地利人损失了越来越多的人。

sentences.en: Basically, they start going backwards.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们开始后撤了。

sentences.en: And day after day, they go backwards.
sentences.zh: 日复一日，他们不断后撤。

sentences.zh: 到12月9日，他们退回了贝尔格莱德。

sentences.zh: 五天后，他们只能说，好吧，游戏又结束了。

sentences.en: There's columns of black smoke rising over villages in the distance, all of this.
sentences.zh: 远处的村庄上空升起阵阵黑烟，诸如此类。

sentences.en: They go past this village called Tannenburg.
sentences.zh: 他们经过了一个叫坦能堡的村庄。

sentences.en: And both generals know their history.
sentences.zh: 两位将军都了解历史。

sentences.en: Because it was here in 1410 that the Teutonic Knights had lost a titanic battle with the Poles and the Lithuanians.
sentences.zh: 因为正是在1410年，条顿骑士团在这里与波兰人和立陶宛人进行了一场惨烈的战役。

sentences.en: And as they're driving back from Tannenburg, they get brilliant news.
sentences.zh: 当他们从坦能堡开车回来时，收到了绝佳的消息。

sentences.en: The Germans have intercepted two Russian radio messages.
sentences.zh: 德国人截获了两条俄军的无线电信息。

sentences.en: Russian communications are terrible.
sentences.zh: 俄军的通讯简直糟糕透顶。

sentences.en: They're not properly disguising their messages.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有对信息进行有效的加密。

sentences.en: Renenkamp and Samsonov are now so far apart that they cannot support each other.
sentences.zh: 伦宁坎普和萨姆索诺夫现在相距太远，无法互相支援。

sentences.en: And Hindenburg says, well, this is our chance.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡说，好了，机会来了。

sentences.en: We'll go for Samsonov.
sentences.zh: 我们要去对付萨姆索诺夫。

sentences.en: We won't just beat him.
sentences.zh: 我们不仅要击败他。

sentences.en: We'll annihilate him.
sentences.zh: 我们要彻底歼灭他。

sentences.en: And when he gets back home, Hindenburg is very General Joffre-like, says to his officers, gentlemen, our preparations are so well in hand that we can all sleep soundly tonight.
sentences.zh: 当兴登堡回到家时，他表现得非常像霞飞将军，他对军官们说，先生们，我们的准备工作已经就绪，今晚大家可以睡个安稳觉了。

sentences.en: And he likes a good night's sleep, doesn't he, Hindenburg?
sentences.zh: 他喜欢睡个好觉，不是吗，兴登堡？

sentences.en: He loves a good night's sleep, as we will discover.
sentences.zh: 他热爱睡个好觉，我们稍后就会发现。

sentences.en: So on the 25th of August, it begins.
sentences.zh: 8月25日，战斗开始了。

sentences.en: Samsonov is pushing these Russians deeper and deeper into the kind of lakelands, into the forests.
sentences.zh: 萨姆索诺夫正驱使俄军深入湖区和森林。

sentences.en: But he has no idea what's out there.
sentences.zh: 但他对外面发生的一切一无所知。

sentences.en: When he hears the first reports of German attacks on the flanks, he doesn't realize that this is a trap.
sentences.zh: 当他听到侧翼遭到德军攻击的初步报告时，他并没有意识到这是一个陷阱。

sentences.en: He says, go deeper, go deeper, keep going.
sentences.zh: 他说，深入，再深入，继续前进。

sentences.en: Now, back at Marienburg, Ludendorff, as always, despite this glacial reputation, he's a nervous wreck.
sentences.zh: 此时在马林堡，鲁登道夫一如既往，尽管他以冷静著称，但实际上他已经精神崩溃了。

sentences.en: So he's beside himself with nerves.
sentences.zh: 他紧张得不知所措。

sentences.en: And actually, at one point, Hindenburg has to take him out of a meeting, take him for a walk to calm him down.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一次兴登堡不得不把他从会议中拉出来，带他去散步以让他冷静下来。

sentences.en: Yeah, because Hindenburg's just puffing on his pipe.
sentences.zh: 没错，因为兴登堡只是在悠闲地抽着烟斗。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: His mustache is drooping.
sentences.zh: 他的胡子都耷拉下来了。

sentences.en: He's mellow.
sentences.zh: 他很从容。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Ludendorff is always sort of sweating and getting very overexcited.
sentences.zh: 鲁登道夫总是那种满头大汗、极度兴奋的样子。

sentences.en: Anyway, everything is actually going according to plan.
sentences.zh: 总之，一切都在按计划进行。

sentences.en: Samsonov is walking deeper and deeper into this.
sentences.zh: 萨姆索诺夫正一步步走进圈套。

sentences.en: So two or three days, he keeps going.
sentences.zh: 接下来的两三天，他一直在前进。

sentences.en: He still doesn't realize, even as the Germans are attacking him on his flanks, what he's doing.
sentences.zh: 即便德军正在攻击他的侧翼，他依然没有意识到自己在做什么。

sentences.en: And then on the 28th of August, so about three or four days into this battle, he realizes that something is wrong.
sentences.zh: 到了8月28日，也就是战斗进行了三四天后，他才意识到出了问题。

sentences.en: Samsonov rides forward to see what's going on.
sentences.zh: 萨姆索诺夫骑马向前查看情况。

sentences.en: And he leaves his communications technology behind, which is a complete disaster for him.
sentences.zh: 但他把通讯设备留在了后面，这对他来说是一场彻底的灾难。

sentences.en: Now, meanwhile, the Germans are closing the trap and they're basically closing in on this army in the foreSt.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，德国人正在收紧陷阱，基本上包围了森林里的这支军队。

sentences.en: Samsonov's men could have maybe got out if they'd immediately withdrawn.
sentences.zh: 如果萨姆索诺夫的部队能立即撤退，或许还有机会逃脱。

sentences.en: Instead, very foolishly, they stand and fight.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们非常愚蠢地选择了原地抵抗。

sentences.en: And that means the Germans are able to cut their lines of retreat and completely surround them.
sentences.zh: 这意味着德国人能够切断他们的撤退路线，并将他们彻底包围。

sentences.en: And so what happens now is a total bloodbath.
sentences.zh: 于是，一场彻底的血腥屠杀发生了。

sentences.en: Thousands upon thousands of the Russians are killed.
sentences.zh: 成千上万的俄军被杀。

sentences.en: The forests are strewn with bodies.
sentences.zh: 森林里到处都是尸体。

sentences.en: For the next two days, they tried to break out.
sentences.zh: 接下来的两天，他们试图突围。

sentences.en: They couldn't.
sentences.zh: 但没能成功。

sentences.en: They're loSt.
sentences.zh: 他们迷路了。

sentences.en: They're disoriented.
sentences.zh: 他们失去了方向感。

sentences.en: They're terrified.
sentences.zh: 他们惊恐万分。

sentences.en: And by the 30th of August, Samsonov's men are surrendering in their thousands.
sentences.zh: 到了8月30日，萨姆索诺夫的部队成千上万地投降了。

sentences.en: Often they're just sitting in the woods with the kind of the hands in the air, hands on their heads, thousands of them waiting to be captured.
sentences.zh: 他们往往只是坐在树林里，举着双手，或者把手放在头上，成千上万的人等待着被俘虏。

sentences.en: The Schlieffen plan had been all about trying to recreate the Battle of Cannae, Hannibal's
sentences.zh: 施里芬计划的核心就是试图重现坎尼会战，即汉尼拔对罗马人的那场伟大胜利，

sentences.en: great victory over the Romans that consisted in surrounding an army and completely annihilating it on the Western Front.
sentences.zh: 那场胜利在于包围并彻底歼灭一支军队，原本是针对西线的。

sentences.en: But as it turns out, the Battle of Cannae is replicated on the Eastern Front at Tannenberg.
sentences.zh: 但事实证明，坎尼会战在东线的坦能堡重演了。

sentences.en: Yeah, very nice.
sentences.zh: 没错，非常精彩。

sentences.en: Exactly the tactic, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 正是这种战术，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Closing the pincers of the trap.
sentences.zh: 合拢陷阱的钳子。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Works brilliantly.
sentences.zh: 效果极佳。

sentences.en: So Hindenburg and Ludendorff, we haven't actually mentioned yet our plan to do an investigative police drama with them as the detectives.
sentences.zh: 所以兴登堡和鲁登道夫，我们还没提到我们计划以他们为主角拍一部调查类警匪剧。

sentences.en: They're going around on trains and they're smoking pipes.
sentences.zh: 他们坐着火车到处走，抽着烟斗。

sentences.en: And then when the need for action comes, they do their stuff.
sentences.zh: 当需要行动时，他们就会大显身手。

sentences.en: I think they'd be brilliant.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他们会非常出色。

sentences.en: But if there's also a crime, they'll solve that on the way.
sentences.zh: 如果路上遇到犯罪案件，他们也会顺手解决。

sentences.en: Anyway, they have taken 92,000 prisoners and they had never imagined such a haul.
sentences.zh: 总之，他们俘虏了9.2万人，这是他们从未想象过的战果。

sentences.en: The Kaiser rather lets himself down at this point.
sentences.zh: 德皇在这一点上表现得相当令人失望。

sentences.en: The Kaiser has a charming plan for the prisoners.
sentences.zh: 德皇对这些俘虏有一个迷人的计划。

sentences.en: He says, I've got a brilliant idea.
sentences.zh: 他说，我有一个绝妙的主意。

sentences.en: Why don't we corral them all on the Corland Peninsula in Western Latvia and starve them all to death?
sentences.zh: 我们为什么不把他们全部关在拉脱维亚西部的库尔兰半岛，然后把他们统统饿死呢？

sentences.en: And actually, even Hindenburg and Ludendorff say, I think that's a bit much.
sentences.zh: 事实上，连兴登堡和鲁登道夫都说，我觉得这有点过分了。

sentences.en: Samsonov, so with his asthma, he escaped in the woods with his entourage, with his Cossack bodyguards.
sentences.zh: 萨姆索诺夫因为哮喘，带着随从和哥萨克保镖逃进了树林。

sentences.en: They left their maps behind very foolishly.
sentences.zh: 他们非常愚蠢地把地图落下了。

sentences.en: So they got completely lost in the woods and they tried to navigate using a compass, like it's basically like sort of Duke of Edinburgh award thing that's gone horribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以他们在树林里彻底迷了路，试图用指南针导航，这简直就像是一场搞砸了的爱丁堡公爵奖励计划活动。

sentences.en: Gone horribly wrong.
sentences.zh: 搞得一团糟。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Samsonov can't breathe.
sentences.zh: 萨姆索诺夫呼吸困难。

sentences.en: He's very depressed.
sentences.zh: 他非常沮丧。

sentences.en: He says to his bodyguards, you know, the emperor trusted me, Nicholas II.
sentences.zh: 他对保镖说，你知道，皇帝尼古拉二世信任我。

sentences.en: How can I ever face him after this disaster?
sentences.zh: 这场灾难之后，我该如何面对他？

sentences.en: And then he basically goes off for a walk into the woods and they hear a gunshot and he's shot himself.
sentences.zh: 然后他独自走进树林，随从们听到了一声枪响，他自杀了。

sentences.en: Oh God, so like Varus after using the three legions.
sentences.zh: 天哪，就像瓦卢斯在损失了三个军团之后一样。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: Back in Germany, total ecstasy.
sentences.zh: 在德国国内，人们陷入了狂喜。

sentences.en: Because this is the point at which the Battle of the Marne has started.
sentences.zh: 因为此时马恩河战役已经打响。

sentences.en: The Western offensive is faltering and the public are desperate for good news.
sentences.zh: 西线的攻势正在受挫，公众迫切需要好消息。

sentences.en: Hindenburg says to the Kaiser, could we please name this after the Battle of Tannenberg?
sentences.zh: 兴登堡对德皇说，我们能以坦能堡战役来命名这场胜利吗？

sentences.en: Because of course they went past the village.
sentences.zh: 因为他们确实经过了那个村庄。

sentences.en: And that gives it tremendous resonance in Germany.
sentences.zh: 这在德国产生了巨大的共鸣。

sentences.en: Though the Teutonic Knights have avenged their historic defeat.
sentences.zh: 条顿骑士团终于洗雪了历史性的战败耻辱。

sentences.en: They've thrown back the Asiatic hordes.
sentences.zh: 他们击退了亚洲蛮族。

sentences.en: The homeland has been saved, all of this.
sentences.zh: 祖国得救了，诸如此类。

sentences.en: The job's not completely done.
sentences.zh: 工作还没有完全结束。

sentences.en: Ten days later, they turn to Rennenkampf in the north, his first army.
sentences.zh: 十天后，他们转向北方的伦宁坎普及其第一集团军。

sentences.en: They try a similar trick, actually, the same trap.
sentences.zh: 他们尝试了类似的诡计，实际上是同样的陷阱。

sentences.en: This time Rennenkampf is expecting it.
sentences.zh: 这一次伦宁坎普有了防备。

sentences.en: He is able to withdraw.
sentences.zh: 他得以撤退。

sentences.en: And so the Russians will end up withdrawing from East Prussia.
sentences.zh: 于是俄军最终从东普鲁士撤离了。

sentences.en: However, they don't leave empty-handed.
sentences.zh: 然而，他们并没有空手而归。

sentences.en: This is another aspect of the story, I think, that people don't know about, by and large, in English-speaking countries.
sentences.zh: 我认为这是故事的另一个方面，在英语国家中，人们大体上并不了解。

sentences.en: As the Russians retreated, they rounded up thousands of people, basically, as hostages.
sentences.zh: 当俄军撤退时，他们抓捕了成千上万的人作为人质。

sentences.en: So Max Hastings tells a very moving story about a family called the Shukas, who lived in a village called Popovon.
sentences.zh: 马克斯·黑斯廷斯讲述了一个关于舒卡一家的感人故事，他们住在波波冯村。

sentences.en: There was a schoolteacher, his wife, and two daughters.
sentences.zh: 家里有一名教师、他的妻子和两个女儿。

sentences.en: Basically, I won't tell you the whole story, but they were taken by the Russians as hostages.
sentences.zh: 基本上，我不讲完整的故事了，但他们被俄军抓走当了人质。

sentences.en: They were taken off to Siberia, and they didn't get home until 1920.
sentences.zh: 他们被带到了西伯利亚，直到1920年才回到家。

sentences.en: Okay, so again, a prefiguring there of the events of the Second World War and its aftermath.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这又是一次对第二次世界大战及其后果的预演。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Well, here's a real prefiguring.
sentences.zh: 好吧，这才是真正的预演。

sentences.en: 10,000 Germans in total were rounded up and deported east in cattle trucks in horrendous conditions when the Russians left East Prussia.
sentences.zh: 当俄军离开东普鲁士时，总共有1万名德国人被抓捕，并被装在牲口车厢里在极其恶劣的条件下被驱逐到东方。

sentences.en: And what is more, I mean, this was a real revelation to me, actually, inside the Russian Empire, there were about 200,000 ethnic Germans, Russian subjects, Russian citizens.
sentences.zh: 而且更重要的是，我的意思是，这对我来说真的是一个巨大的启示，实际上，在俄罗斯帝国境内，大约有20万名德裔居民，他们是俄罗斯的臣民，也是俄罗斯公民。

sentences.en: They were deported east as well.
sentences.zh: 他们也被流放到了东方。

sentences.en: Some historians think maybe as many as half of them died from disease, cold, starvation, and so on, in the years that followed.
sentences.zh: 一些历史学家认为，在随后的几年里，他们中可能有多达一半的人死于疾病、严寒、饥饿等等。

sentences.en: I mean, this is a story that most of us, I guess, have never heard of.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我想我们大多数人可能从未听说过这个故事。

sentences.en: Well, this is not the end at all of the campaign in the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这根本不是东线战役的终点。

sentences.en: No, we've got three years to go, right?
sentences.zh: 不，我们还有三年要打，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And the really confusing thing about all this is that a few weeks later, the Russians came back, and they actually won some really big victories that nobody's ever heard of.
sentences.zh: 关于这一切，真正令人困惑的是，几周后，俄军卷土重来，他们实际上赢得了一些鲜为人知的重大胜利。

sentences.en: The Battle of the Vistula, the Battle of Łódź.
sentences.zh: 维斯瓦河战役，罗兹战役。

sentences.en: The Battle of what?
sentences.zh: 什么战役？

sentences.en: Łódź.
sentences.zh: 罗兹。

sentences.en: It's an industrial town in sort of south-central Poland.
sentences.zh: 那是波兰中南部的一个工业城镇。

sentences.en: No, I've literally never heard of that.
sentences.zh: 不，我真的从来没听说过那个地方。

sentences.en: It's spelled L-O-D-Z.
sentences.zh: 拼写是L-O-D-Z。

sentences.en: You've seen that word.
sentences.zh: 你见过这个词。

sentences.en: Lodz.
sentences.zh: 罗兹。

sentences.en: Yeah, you've seen that written down.
sentences.zh: 是的，你见过它被写下来。

sentences.en: I think Lodz is how you pronounce it, Tom.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我觉得应该读作“罗兹”。

sentences.en: No, I think not, Tom.
sentences.zh: 不，我不这么认为，汤姆。

sentences.en: Łódź.
sentences.zh: Łódź。

sentences.en: Now, putting that on one side, Hindenburg and Ludendorff are the huge winners from this.
sentences.zh: 好了，把这个先放一边，兴登堡和鲁登道夫是这场战役的最大赢家。

sentences.en: Hindenburg becomes a national idol, almost unmatched, I think, in any other country.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡成为了民族偶像，我想在任何其他国家都几乎无人能及。

sentences.en: So in Berlin, people put up a 39-foot wooden statue of him.
sentences.zh: 所以在柏林，人们为他竖起了一座39英尺高的木制雕像。

sentences.en: This is one of the nail men.
sentences.zh: 这就是所谓的“钉子人”之一。

sentences.en: This is so interesting.
sentences.zh: 这太有趣了。

sentences.en: You put up these statues made of wood, and then you'd pay to hammer in a nail, and the money would go to the armed forces.
sentences.zh: 你竖起这些木制雕像，然后人们花钱往上面钉钉子，钱则捐给武装部队。

sentences.en: So there were hundreds of these nail men across Germany and Austria.
sentences.zh: 所以当时德国和奥地利各地有数百个这样的“钉子人”。

sentences.en: You'd have Siegfried.
sentences.zh: 你可以有齐格弗里德。

sentences.en: You'd have Charlemagne.
sentences.zh: 你可以有查理大帝。

sentences.en: You'd have Roland.
sentences.zh: 你可以有罗兰。

sentences.en: You'd have Henry the Lion.
sentences.zh: 你可以有狮子亨利。

sentences.en: Otto the Great.
sentences.zh: 奥托大帝。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you'd hammer in your nail, you know, and raise money for the war effort.
sentences.zh: 你往上面钉钉子，你知道的，为战争筹集资金。

sentences.en: Now, some German officers thought this was mad to give Hindenburg so much credit.
sentences.zh: 现在，一些德国军官认为把这么多功劳归于兴登堡简直是疯了。

sentences.en: They said he's basically a clapped-out, pipe-smoking walrus who's taking the credit for other people's successes.
sentences.zh: 他们说他基本上就是一头抽着烟斗、精疲力竭的海象，却在窃取别人的成功果实。

sentences.en: And Ludendorff's deputy, later on, used to give tours of the Battle of Tannenburg.
sentences.zh: 后来，鲁登道夫的副官经常带人参观坦能堡战役遗址。

sentences.en: He was called Max Hoffman.
sentences.zh: 他叫马克斯·霍夫曼。

sentences.en: And he would say, this is where Field Marshal Hindenburg slept before the battle, this is where he slept after the battle, and this is where he slept during the battle.
sentences.zh: 他会说，这是兴登堡元帅战前睡觉的地方，这是他战后睡觉的地方，这是他战斗期间睡觉的地方。

sentences.en: Is that fair?
sentences.zh: 这公平吗？

sentences.en: No, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实不公平。

sentences.en: So, clearly, Ludendorff is the real genius.
sentences.zh: 所以，很明显，鲁登道夫才是真正的天才。

sentences.en: Ludendorff is the master of detail.
sentences.zh: 鲁登道夫是细节大师。

sentences.zh: 当然，问题在于，他们在20世纪20年代和30年代的后期行为玷污了他们的名声，当时他们的表现确实令人不齿。

sentences.zh: 他们建立了一个叫“东方战区司令部”（Oberost）的机构。

sentences.en: And that basically meant that they were now military dictators, these two guys, of the Baltic and of Belarus and Eastern Poland, of the areas that were occupied by the Germans.
sentences.zh: 这基本上意味着这两个家伙现在成了波罗的海、白俄罗斯和波兰东部这些被德国占领地区的军事独裁者。

sentences.zh: 一些历史学家说这是纳粹主义的预演，因为他们的行为非常严酷和压迫，而且对斯拉夫人表现出完全的蔑视。

sentences.en: I don't think that's fair.

sentences.zh: 我不认为这是纳粹主义的预演。

sentences.zh: 我认为，尽管他们压迫且冷酷，但他们并非种族灭绝。

sentences.en: They don't have any, you know, program of kind of, you know, racial hygiene, as the Nazis would have called it.
sentences.zh: 他们没有任何，你知道的，纳粹所称的那种“种族卫生”计划。

sentences.en: They're killing people in the East, but not for Nazi reasons.
sentences.zh: 他们在东方杀人，但不是出于纳粹的动机。

sentences.zh: 是的，没错。

sentences.zh: 他们杀人是出于军事原因。

sentences.zh: 现在，德皇假装对这一切感到欣喜若狂。

sentences.zh: 他访问了东方战区司令部去给他们晋升。

sentences.zh: 所以兴登堡成了元帅等等。

sentences.en: But the Kaiser is absolutely smouldering with jealousy.
sentences.zh: 但德皇内心却因嫉妒而怒火中烧。

sentences.zh: 他真的很嫉妒兴登堡，而且极其鄙视鲁登道夫。

sentences.en: He says he's a dubious character, eaten away by personal ambition.
sentences.zh: 他说他是一个可疑的人物，被个人野心所吞噬。

sentences.en: What great things is he supposed to have accomplished?
sentences.zh: 他到底完成了什么伟大的成就？

sentences.en: I mean, that's rich coming from the Kaiser.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这话从德皇嘴里说出来真是讽刺。

sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，击败了俄国人。

sentences.en: Yeah, defeat the Russians, exactly.
sentences.zh: 是的，击败了俄国人，没错。

sentences.en: And, of course, the great irony is that by the end of the war, the Kaiser will become their puppet.
sentences.zh: 当然，最大的讽刺是，到战争结束时，德皇将成为他们的傀儡。

sentences.en: Because that's the real legacy of the Battle of Tannenberg.
sentences.zh: 因为这就是坦能堡战役真正的遗产。

sentences.en: It gives power to these two men who think the war can be won on the battlefield, not with a negotiated settlement.
sentences.zh: 它赋予了这两个人权力，他们认为战争可以在战场上赢得，而不是通过谈判解决。

sentences.en: So you could argue that in the long run, Tannenberg is a disaster for Germany.
sentences.zh: 所以你可以说，从长远来看，坦能堡对德国来说是一场灾难。

sentences.en: It would be better for the Germans not to have won it, in a way.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，德国人没赢下那场战役可能会更好。

sentences.en: Because their war would have been over more quickly, perhaps, with some form of negotiation.
sentences.zh: 因为也许通过某种形式的谈判，他们的战争会更快结束。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: And in the very long run, Tannenberg has a properly baleful afterlife.
sentences.zh: 而且从极长远来看，坦能堡有着极其恶劣的后世影响。

sentences.en: Because in 1927, the Germans built this huge memorial on the battlefield with eight towers.
sentences.zh: 因为在1927年，德国人在战场上建造了这个巨大的八塔纪念碑。

sentences.en: It was modelled on a cross between a Teutonic castle and the castle of Frederick II in Apulia, in Italy.
sentences.zh: 它的设计灵感来源于条顿城堡和意大利普利亚腓特烈二世城堡的结合体。

sentences.en: Hindenberg dedicated it personally before thousands and thousands of veterans.
sentences.zh: 兴登堡在成千上万的老兵面前亲自为它揭幕。

sentences.en: And he gave this incredibly nationalistic speech in which he said, the First World War was a noble crusade.
sentences.zh: 他发表了一场极其民族主义的演讲，在演讲中他说，第一次世界大战是一场高尚的十字军东征。

sentences.en: You know, we were on the right side.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们站在正义的一方。

sentences.en: For the Nazis, Tannenberg was a huge deal.
sentences.zh: 对于纳粹来说，坦能堡意义重大。

sentences.en: In the first year, Hitler went.
sentences.zh: 第一年，希特勒就去了。

sentences.en: All the big names went.
sentences.zh: 所有大人物都去了。

sentences.en: They had torch-lit parades.
sentences.zh: 他们举行了火炬游行。

sentences.en: When Hindenberg died in 1934, he was buried there.
sentences.zh: 1934年兴登堡去世时，他被安葬在那里。

sentences.en: An even bigger deal, more torch-lit parades.
sentences.zh: 规模更大，更多的火炬游行。

sentences.en: There was a shrine, basically a Nazi shrine, with these two huge granite soldiers called the Eternal Watch.
sentences.zh: 那里有一个圣殿，基本上是纳粹的圣殿，有两座巨大的花岗岩士兵雕像，被称为“永恒守望”。

sentences.en: Oh, so like the Valle de los Cados.
sentences.zh: 哦，就像烈士谷那样。

sentences.zh: 或者像《指环王》里的阿尔戈纳斯之柱。

sentences.zh: 你知道的，安都因河上的那两座雕像。

sentences.zh: 但他们是好人，不是吗？

sentences.zh: 他们是好人，所以这是一个糟糕的比较。

sentences.zh: 但当德国人在1945年从东普鲁士撤退时，整个建筑群被德国士兵炸毁了。

sentences.en: And then every single trace was erased by the Polish communists afterwards, so that today nothing of it remains at all.
sentences.zh: 随后，波兰共产党人抹去了每一处痕迹，以至于今天那里什么都没剩下。

sentences.en: That is looking far ahead into the future.
sentences.zh: 那是对未来的长远展望。

sentences.zh: 但现在，我们还停留在1914年。

sentences.zh: 所以，在今天的节目中，总结一下，奥地利人在塞尔维亚把事情搞得一团糟。

sentences.zh: 它会为我们这期关于1914年战争的系列节目提供最后一集吗？

sentences.zh: 确实会，汤姆，而且这是所有故事中最戏剧性的一个。

sentences.en: Tolkien's fantasy classic, The Hobbit.
sentences.zh: 敬请欣赏。

sentences.en: Enjoy.
sentences.zh: 他看见有人在水那边的树林里点火。

sentences.en: He sees someone light a fire in the wood beyond the water.
sentences.zh: 有一瞬间，他想到了掠夺成性的巨龙降落在自己安静的山丘上，点燃祭坛之火。

sentences.en: For a moment, he thought of plundering dragons settling on his quiet hill and kindling altar flames.
sentences.zh: 他打了个寒颤。

sentences.en: He shuddered.
sentences.zh: 很快，他又变回了那个住在袋底洞的巴金斯先生。

sentences.en: Very quickly, he was playing Mr. Baggins of Bag End Underhill again.
sentences.zh: 现在，问题是，托尔金是在20世纪30年代写下这段话的。

sentences.en: Now, the thing is, Tolkien's writing this in the 1930s.
sentences.zh: 我认为那段文字完美地捕捉到了20世纪20年代和30年代许多英国人的心态。

sentences.en: And I think that paragraph perfectly captures the sensibility of so many British people in the 1920s and 1930s.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，第一次世界大战已经发生，他们已经回家了。

sentences.en: In other words, the First World War has happened and they've come home.
sentences.zh: 对于像托尔金这样的人来说，第一次世界大战意味着他们再也不会把战争看作是浪漫的、迷人的、无痛的，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And for people like Tolkien, the First World War means that they never think of war again as romantic, as glamorous, as pain-free, all of that stuff.
sentences.zh: 托尔金只想待在家里打理他的花园，不想卷入其中。

sentences.en: Tolkien just wants to stay at home and tend his garden and not get involved.
sentences.zh: 现在，他内心有一部分确实感到被冒险和刺激所吸引。

sentences.en: Now, there is a bit of him that feels pulled towards adventure and excitement.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他们担心如果卷入远离家乡的事务，巨龙就会来烧毁他们的家园、村庄和城镇。

sentences.en: But at the same time, they're worried that if they get involved in matters far from home, dragons will come and set fire to their homes, their villages, their towns.
sentences.zh: 你在这个播客的前面提到了斯坦利·鲍德温。

sentences.en: And you had a fleeting mention earlier in this podcast of Stanley Baldwin.
sentences.zh: 斯坦利·鲍德温非常像霍比特人，他喜欢穿马甲，他来自这个地区，伍斯特郡。

sentences.en: And Stanley Baldwin, who's very Hobbit-like, he likes a waistcoat, he's from this part of the world, from Worcestershire.
sentences.zh: 他确实是一种新型的政治家，我想是不浪漫的，不迷人的。

sentences.en: He is very much a new kind of politician who's unromantic, I suppose, unglamorous.
sentences.zh: 他曾有名言说，你知道的，“轰炸机总会突破防线”，意思是，要担心轰炸，你知道的，一场新的战争将是末日般的，诸如此类的事情。

sentences.en: And he famously says, you know, the bomber will always get through, as in, be worried about bombing, you know, a new war would be apocalyptic and all of that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 我认为比尔博完全体现了那种张力。

sentences.en: And I think Bilbo, he absolutely embodies that tension.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他内心有一部分被冒险和刺激所吸引。

sentences.en: You know, there's part of him that is pulled towards adventure and pulled towards excitement.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他很焦虑，他热爱家庭，他很害怕。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he's anxious, he's home-loving, he's frightened.
sentences.zh: 我认为他是托尔金写作时那一代人心态的完美写照。

sentences.en: He's a kind of perfect representation, I think, of the mentality of so many people of Tolkien's generation at the time that he was writing.
sentences.zh: 但我还觉得有趣的是，显然，《指环王》是后来才写的。

sentences.en: But I also think it's interesting that, obviously, The Lord of the Rings was written a bit later.
sentences.zh: 所以当这段文字被写下时，战争的乌云已经在某种程度上出现在地平线上，但还没有聚集在头顶上方。

sentences.en: So when this is being written, the storm clouds of war are kind of, they're on the horizon, but they're not yet gathering above.
sentences.zh: 所以当这段文字被写下时，战争的乌云已经在某种程度上出现在地平线上，但还没有聚集在头顶上方。

sentences.en: And Bilbo isn't forced out of his comfortable life in Hobbit Hole because he knows that he has to do something to save his homeland.
sentences.zh: 比尔博并非因为知道自己必须拯救家园，才被迫离开霍比特洞那舒适的生活。

sentences.en: He doesn't go because he knows there's darkness beyond the gates that he could play a part in quelling and destroying.
sentences.zh: 他之所以出发，并不是因为他知道门外有黑暗势力，而他能参与平定和摧毁这些势力。

sentences.en: In The Hobbit, the stakes aren't that high.
sentences.zh: 在《霍比特人》中，赌注并没有那么大。

sentences.en: There isn't an existential threat at the door yet.
sentences.zh: 门外还没有出现生存威胁。

sentences.en: It's just about reclaiming something that was loSt.
sentences.zh: 这只是为了夺回一些失去的东西。

sentences.en: Whereas Frodo in The Lord of the Rings has to go out and save the world.
sentences.zh: 而《指环王》中的弗罗多则必须挺身而出，拯救世界。

sentences.en: And The Lord of the Rings was probably written at a time when, you know, the threat of the Nazis was unavoidable.
sentences.zh: 《指环王》大概是在纳粹威胁迫在眉睫的时期写成的。

sentences.en: The wolf was at the door.
sentences.zh: 当时大难临头，危机四伏。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's much less existential in The Hobbit.
sentences.zh: 没错，《霍比特人》中的生存危机感确实要小得多。

sentences.en: It's actually the love of exploration and adventure.
sentences.zh: 它实际上更多是关于对探索和冒险的热爱。

sentences.en: And I guess to some extent, the story of The Hobbit, it's all about Bilbo finding his courage, really.
sentences.zh: 我想在某种程度上，《霍比特人》的故事其实就是关于比尔博如何找到勇气的过程。

sentences.en: Not physical courage, because he never really fights in battles and does all those things.
sentences.zh: 不是那种身体上的勇气，因为他从未真正参与过战斗或做过那些事。

sentences.en: In fact, there's a lovely moment, actually.
sentences.zh: 事实上，有一个非常动人的时刻。

sentences.en: The critic Tom Shippey mentions it, and I thought, gosh, this is so true.
sentences.zh: 评论家汤姆·希皮提到过这一点，我当时想，天哪，这说得太对了。

sentences.en: The bravest thing that Bilbo ever does is much later on, he's on his own, he's in a tunnel, and he's going to see Smaug.
sentences.zh: 比尔博做过的最勇敢的事发生在很久之后，当时他独自一人在隧道里，准备去见史矛革。

sentences.en: The dwarves have sent him, and the narrator says, this was the bravest thing he ever did.
sentences.zh: 矮人们派他去，叙述者说，这是他做过最勇敢的事。

sentences.en: The tremendous thing that happened afterwards was nothing.
sentences.zh: 后来发生的那些惊天动地的事情反而不算什么了。

sentences.en: He fought the real battle in that tunnel alone before he ever saw the vast danger that lay in wait.
sentences.zh: 他在那条隧道里独自打赢了真正的战斗，甚至在他看到潜伏的巨大危险之前。

sentences.en: And I thought, the man who's written those words is a man who stood in a trench with his mates, waiting for the whistle.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，写下这些文字的人，一定曾和战友们一起站在战壕里，等待着冲锋的哨声。

sentences.en: They had no idea what was on the other side.
sentences.zh: 他们根本不知道对面等待着什么。

sentences.en: But that dark night of the soul, that kind of moment when you know you're about to go into battle, but you don't know what's waiting, and you have to go, you have to overcome it.
sentences.zh: 但那种灵魂的至暗时刻，那种你知道即将投入战斗，却不知道等待你的是什么，而你必须去面对、必须去克服的时刻。

sentences.en: Overcome yourself, yeah.
sentences.zh: 克服你自己，没错。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: So that, to me, is some of the modernity of The Hobbit.
sentences.zh: 所以，对我来说，这就是《霍比特人》现代性的一部分。

sentences.en: That it's written by somebody who doesn't think that war is all exciting and glamorous.
sentences.zh: 它是出自一个不认为战争是激动人心、光彩夺目的人之手。

sentences.en: That's a really interesting thing that Tolkien does throughout.
sentences.zh: 托尔金始终贯穿这一点，这非常有意思。

sentences.en: He situates you in an imaginary world in order to tell you something about the realities of our world.
sentences.zh: 他把你置于一个虚构的世界，以此来告诉你关于我们现实世界的一些真相。

sentences.en: In other words, adventures are not heroic and exciting.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，冒险并不总是英雄主义和令人兴奋的。

sentences.en: They're often just really uncomfortable.
sentences.zh: 它们往往只是让人非常不舒服。

sentences.en: There's a lot of sitting in the rain, and there's a lot of not getting dinner.
sentences.zh: 有很多时候要在雨中坐着，还有很多时候没饭吃。

sentences.en: The goodies don't necessarily come out of winning better people.
sentences.zh: 好人并不一定会因为胜利而变得更好。

sentences.en: Winning often makes them worse people.
sentences.zh: 胜利往往会让他们变得更糟。

sentences.en: Heroes don't instinctively run headfirst into battle.
sentences.zh: 英雄不会本能地一头扎进战斗中。

sentences.en: They have a sense of their mortality and fear as much as the rest of us.
sentences.zh: 他们和我们其他人一样，有对死亡的恐惧和认知。

sentences.en: They do.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: Anyway, Bilbo is nevertheless dragged into the adventure by Gandalf, and Gandalf must be one of the most iconic characters of any fantasy series ever.
sentences.zh: 总之，比尔博还是被甘道夫拖进了这场冒险，甘道夫一定是所有奇幻系列中最具标志性的人物之一。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，没错。

sentences.en: I mean, he is the original Dumbledore, right?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他是邓布利多的原型，对吧？

sentences.en: He's a version of Merlin, though, don't you think?
sentences.zh: 不过，你不觉得他是梅林的一个版本吗？

sentences.en: He's less dark.
sentences.zh: 他没那么阴暗。

sentences.en: He's got a lot more humour to him, a lot more twinkle.
sentences.zh: 他更有幽默感，眼里闪烁着更多的智慧光芒。

sentences.en: He's more fallible.
sentences.zh: 他更容易犯错。

sentences.en: But yeah, I would say in the way that Merlin guides the quest, so does Gandalf.
sentences.zh: 但没错，我会说就像梅林指引探险一样，甘道夫也是如此。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He's like the dwarves' manager.
sentences.zh: 他就像是矮人们的经纪人。

sentences.en: He is.
sentences.zh: 确实是。

sentences.en: And he's basically recruited Bilbo very much against his will to be a burglar for them.
sentences.zh: 而且他基本上是在比尔博极不情愿的情况下，招募他来当他们的飞贼。

sentences.en: And actually, sometimes people, frankly, who I think don't know what they're talking about, say, oh, I don't think Tolkien's a very good writer,
sentences.zh: 坦率地说，有时有些人——我认为他们根本不知道自己在说什么——会说，哦，我不觉得托尔金是个好作家，

sentences.en: because actually they don't like the songs or whatever it might be.
sentences.zh: 因为他们不喜欢书里的歌谣什么的。

sentences.en: Actually, when you look at those first chapters, Tolkien's a great writer, because he completely captures the different characters and almost the different kind of
sentences.zh: 实际上，当你读那些前几章时，会发现托尔金是一位伟大的作家，因为他通过人物的说话方式，完全捕捉到了不同角色的性格，甚至捕捉到了他们各自的

sentences.en: temporal registers of the characters through the way they speak.
sentences.zh: 时间语境。

sentences.en: So Bilbo is very modern.
sentences.zh: 所以比尔博非常现代。

sentences.en: Bilbo speaks in a modern, middle-class way.
sentences.zh: 比尔博说话的方式很现代，很有中产阶级的味道。

sentences.en: So we see in Bilbo, as you said, he's a bridge to this world.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，我们在比尔博身上看到了他作为通往这个世界桥梁的作用。

sentences.en: And if you want to hear the full episode, you just need to sign up to the Rest is History
sentences.zh: 如果你想收听完整节目，只需注册《Rest is History》即可。

sentences.en: Club at therestishistory.com.
sentences.zh: Club at therestishistory.com.

sentences.en: And not only will you get access to this thrilling new show, but you get all the usual benefits.
sentences.zh: 你不仅可以收听这个精彩的新节目，还能享受所有常规福利。

sentences.en: You get the ad-free listening, the early access to episodes, the bonus episodes.
sentences.zh: 你可以享受无广告收听、抢先收听剧集以及额外奖励剧集。

sentences.en: And if you're not a massive fan of The Hobbit, don't despair, because in the next couple of
sentences.zh: 如果你不是《霍比特人》的超级粉丝，也不要灰心，因为在接下来的几周里，

sentences.en: weeks, we'll be doing Bram Stoker's Chilling Dracula, and we'll be doing Margaret Atwood's dystopian fable, The Handmaid's Tale.
sentences.zh: 我们将制作布莱姆·斯托克的惊悚作品《德古拉》，以及玛格丽特·阿特伍德的反乌托邦寓言《使女的故事》。

sentences.en: Bye-bye.
sentences.zh: 再见。
